name: Request path
blurb: Every hop a single public request takes, numbered in reading order, and what each one checks. The turn at hop 7 is where the request leaves the public plane and re-enters FLEX through the private API.
audience: On-call, and anyone tracing a live request
note: Hops 2a and 2b both act on the viewer request at the edge — nothing in this repository fixes which of them runs first, so they are drawn side by side rather than in sequence. Hops 9a and 9b are alternatives, and one request may make several of them, in sequence or in parallel. Everything from hop 6 onwards runs inside the VPC; the tiers themselves live on the Network tab.

tables.name: Retry and failure semantics
tables.note: Retries are opt-in and nothing on the internal path opts in, so every domain to private-API to gateway call is single-attempt.
rows: retryAttempts per integration or per call, capped at 6
maxRetryDelay per integration or per call, clamped to 10–1000 ms
not configurable — retryAttempts is not in the integration schema
only the DVLA gateway uses the public fetcher

d.tech: CloudFront · AWS WAF v2 · CloudFront Functions
d.role: Everything that runs before CloudFront makes the origin request.
facts: The Web ACL, both CloudFront Functions and the distribution are created by FlexGlobalStack, which pins env.region to us-east-1.

d.role: The public API and the two Lambdas it invokes directly.
facts: The boundary drawn here is the region, not the VPC — the authorizer and every domain route function also run inside the VPC.

d.tech: API Gateway REST · PRIVATE endpoint · IAM auth
d.role: Reachable only through the API Gateway interface endpoint inside the VPC.
facts: Nothing in here has a hostname an external caller can usefully reach: the private API's resource policy denies every principal whose aws:SourceVpce is not the interface endpoint.

d.role: Sends the request with a Cognito access token in the Authorization header.
Managed rules, IP reputation and a per-IP rate limit.
facts: Attached to the distribution as its Web ACL; managed rules, IP reputation and the rate rule are evaluated at the edge before the cache.
Default action is allow. Five rules in priority order: common rule set, known bad inputs, an x-flex-e2e-bypass header allow, IP reputation, then a 2000-per-IP rate limit.
Data protection substitutes the authorization header out of WAF logs and sampled requests.

d.role: Stamps a correlation ID, then structurally validates the bearer token.
facts: Fails on: missing header, no Bearer prefix, extra segments, wrong JWT segment count, header or body that isn't JSON, alg:none. The signature is only checked for presence.
Emits cff_token_missing or cff_token_invalid on failure, cff_token_validated on success.
Rejections are a 401 carrying x-rejected-by: cloudfront-function, returned from the edge.

d.role: Adds the x-origin-verify header and forwards to the regional API origin.
facts: Caching is disabled on the API behaviour, so every request reaches the eu-west-2 origin.
originPath is /prod, so the origin sees the stage name in front of every path.
The /docs* behaviour is a different origin, function and cache policy entirely — it is not on this path.

d.tech: AWS WAF v2 · REGIONAL scope, associated to the prod stage
d.role: Default block; allows only requests carrying the origin secret.
facts: This is the hop that makes the API Gateway URL unusable directly — disableExecuteApiEndpoint is never set, so the execute-api host still resolves; the Web ACL is what stops it.
Two rules only: the known-bad-inputs managed group, then the byte match that allows.

d.role: Matches the resource under /app/{domain}/{version}/… and triggers the token authorizer.
facts: Two gateway responses are re-templated: UNAUTHORIZED to 401 and ACCESS_DENIED to 403, both echoing $context.authorizer.errorMessage.

d.tech: Lambda · NODEJS_24_X · Middy stack · typed route context
d.role: Validates the request, runs the handler, validates the response.
facts: Body and query are Zod-validated before the handler runs; declared headers are only checked for presence (a missing required header is a 400). A body schema on a GET route is silently ignored.
A response that fails the route's response schema is logged, emits response_validation_failed, and is replaced with a 500 — the handler's payload is not returned.
Throws AuthorizationError (401) when pairwiseId is absent from the authorizer context. Only public routes get a ctx.auth at all.
Independent upstream calls are issued together: the dvla routes fetch the linking ID and the DVLA session token in one Promise.all before calling the gateway.

d.role: Verifies the access token's signature, issuer, token_use and client ID.
facts: Expired tokens get a distinct message (JWT expired) on the 403 access-denied response; everything else is a plain deny with no message. The 401 UNAUTHORIZED response only fires when API Gateway rejects before invoking the authorizer.
Returns the token's username claim as pairwiseId in the authorizer context; the allow policy it returns names *, not the invoked method.
Runs in the VPC's egress tier and fetches the Cognito JWKS out over NAT — in development, a stub JWKS Function URL instead.

nodes.label: 8. Private REST API
nodes.sub: PRIVATE endpoint · IAM auth · interface endpoint only

facts: The resource policy is a single DENY on every principal whose aws:SourceVpce is not the API Gateway interface endpoint. There is no explicit allow, so for same-account callers the caller's own IAM policy is the sole gate.
Every method is AuthorizationType.IAM.
No ctx.auth on private routes — where identity is needed it is passed as an explicitly declared header, by convention a required User-Id.
The same SDK pipeline as hop 7 runs here, so the 400/500 validation behaviour is identical.

d.role: Strips the prefix, looks the route up in code, resolves its secret, builds a typed client.
facts: The consumer config comes from Secrets Manager with a 600-second cache and is Zod-parsed, so a malformed config fails the Lambda at first use rather than at deploy.
An upstream response that fails the route's declared schema becomes a 502.
Consumer credentials never leave the gateway Lambda — with one exception: DVLA's session token, which the domain fetches at hop 7 and sends back on every subsequent call.

d.role: Driving licence, customer vehicle, share code and vehicle enquiry services.
facts: Reached over the internet through a NAT gateway rather than a private endpoint — the DVLA gateway function is placed in the egress tier for exactly this, unlike the udp and uns gateways.

d.role: Systems of record for identity links, users, preferences, groups and notifications.
facts: Both gateway functions sit in isolated subnets with no NAT route. Each dials a URL taken from its consumer-config secret — udp's apiUrl, uns's privateApiUrl — neither of which is in this repository, so reachability depends on that URL resolving inside AWS.
httpVersion is never set on the distribution, so CDK's HTTP2 default applies; minimumProtocolVersion is TLS_V1_2_2021.
Drawn as a fork rather than a sequence on purpose: nothing in this repository fixes whether the Web ACL or the viewer-request function is evaluated first. Both must pass.
The rate rule blocks at 2000 requests per IP; a blocked request is answered from the edge and never reaches an origin.

d.carries: The request with a guaranteed correlation ID
facts: A v4 UUID supplied by the caller is reused; otherwise one is derived by SHA-256 from the CloudFront request ID.
The origin request policy is ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER, so the Authorization header and the correlation ID both reach the origin.

d.auth: Exact byte match on the x-origin-verify header
facts: The secret is a 32-character generated Secrets Manager value replicated into us-east-1 so the distribution and the Web ACL read the same string.

d.carries: The raw Authorization header out; an IAM policy plus pairwiseId back
facts: resultsCacheTtl is never set, so API Gateway caches the decision for CDK's five-minute default, keyed by the token — most requests do not invoke the authorizer at all.

d.carries: The proxy event, including the authorizer context
facts: One function per route: each declared method under /app/{domain}/{version}/{path} binds to its own NodejsFunction.

edges.label: the turn · SigV4 into the private API

d.protocol: HTTPS through the API Gateway interface endpoint
d.auth: SigV4 signed with the route function's own execution role
d.carries: A /domains/… or /gateways/… request — the request re-entering FLEX from the inside
facts: flexFetch supports exponential backoff with full jitter up to 6 attempts, but retries are opt-in and nothing on this path opts in — every domain → private API → gateway call is single-attempt. Only the DVLA gateway's outbound internet calls retry, via createPublicFetch's default of 3.

The role's inline policy names only the route ARNs its declared integrations resolve to, and the permissions boundary denies lambda:InvokeFunction outright — which is why this turn exists instead of a direct invoke.

The dvla domain makes this turn twice for most routes: once to GET /v1/authenticate for a session token, then again with that token as a required auth header — so a DVLA bearer token does traverse the domain Lambda and the private API.

Nothing carries the platform's x-correlation-id across this turn: buildHeaders injects it only when the route store holds a header declared under the key x-correlation-id, and no domain config declares one. The correlation chain ends at hop 7.

d.auth: IAM · execute-api:Invoke on that route's ARN
IAM · execute-api:Invoke on that route's ARN
facts: One {proxy+} method per gateway: the gateway Lambda, not API Gateway, decides which upstream operation the remaining path means.

edges.label: a target domain may call a gateway too

d.protocol: HTTPS back out through the private API
facts: udp calls the dvla gateway; groups calls the udp and uns gateways. (uns reaches udp as a domain call, not a gateway call.)

d.auth: An API key plus a DVLA-issued bearer token, over an unsigned client
d.carries: A DVLA operation, mapped from the inbound proxy path
facts: Every DVLA route except authenticate and the JWKS fetch sends X-API-KEY alongside the Authorization header the domain obtained at hop 7.
The gateway mints a fresh X-Correlation-Id per client build instead of propagating one, and caches the DVLA JWKS in a module-scope variable across warm invocations.

d.auth: sts:AssumeRole then SigV4, plus an API key header — x-api-key for UDP, X-API-KEY for UNS
facts: The assumed-role credential provider is memoised in a module-level Map so warm invocations reuse the STS session instead of re-assuming per request.
